clue.text: Matilda, a novel in a coastal region

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of the name and the article are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Roald Dahl's Matilda is described as a novel set somewhere by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the noun for the book Matilda, but here it means 'new' and tells you to rearrange MATILDA plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is the strip of Croatian shoreline along the Adriatic, a coastal region.

clue.text: Blessed, always noble, saved from the guillotine

parts.note: blessed and darn are both mild oaths, as in 'the darn thing'
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A sanctified, ever-aristocratic figure is rescued from execution.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Darnay, a French aristocrat in A Tale of Two Cities, is rescued from the guillotine by Sydney Carton.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darnay, heir to the Evrémonde title, is spared the guillotine when Carton takes his place.

clue.text: Tizzy after university replaces a theology professor

indicators.note: replaces means the letter for university is put in place of the a

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be in a tizzy

explanation.surface: An academic in divinity is thrown into a state when a university intervenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: U replaces the A of LATHER. Martin Luther taught theology at Wittenberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther held the chair of biblical theology at Wittenberg before the Reformation.

clue.text: In song, US subject Ethel's heading home to Joseph

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
math is the American short form of mathematics, a school subject

indicators.note: heading means only the first letter of Ethel's

explanation.surface: An American singer named Ethel croons about returning home to Joseph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In song' suggests singing, but the song is the container; 'US subject' points to the American short form of mathematics. Joseph of Arimathea gave his tomb for Jesus's burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph of Arimathea is named after his home town in the Gospels.

clue.text: Island vehicle opening up to admit press writer from Russia

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: to admit means the turned word lets the next word inside
up in a down clue means this word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a vent is an opening
to press is to urge

explanation.surface: A vehicle on an island opens up to let in a journalist from Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the opening to give TNEV, and 'to admit' sets the press synonym inside it after the T. Ivan Turgenev wrote Fathers and Sons.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist, author of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Love along with The Shiralee author

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, so nil
along with means and

explanation.surface: A reader declares affection for an Australian novel and its writer.
explanation.walkthrough: D'Arcy Niland was the Australian author of The Shiralee (1955).
explanation.definitionFit: D'Arcy Niland wrote the Australian novel The Shiralee, so he is its author.

clue.text: Johnson's play, one a French novelist called "Ballet"

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
René Ballet was a French novelist, so his first name is René

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's drama is credited to a French writer nicknamed Ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson's only play was the tragedy Irene (1749).
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is the tragedy Samuel Johnson wrote, staged by Garrick in 1749.

clue.text: A holiday bar opening in summer

indicators.note: bar opening means stop the first letter, removing it from the word

parts.note: a festival is a holiday or feast day

explanation.surface: A summer bank holiday sees a pub opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' means 'except' here, not a pub: FESTIVAL less its first letter. Aestival means of or occurring in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aestival is a formal adjective meaning of or in the summer season, from Latin aestas.

clue.text: Muck spoilt one's rooms in Château d'If

parts.note: dung is muck, manure

indicators.note: spoilt means damaged and rearranged, so the letters of one's are mixed up

explanation.surface: Filth has ruined someone's quarters in the island fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The Château d'If is the island prison where Edmond Dantès is held in The Count of Monte Cristo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Château d'If is a fortress prison, so its rooms are cells in underground vaults.

clue.text: Rogue horse — it flipped over a playwright

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or rogue

indicators.note: flipped over tells you to turn the horse and the word it backwards together

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild horse throws its rider on top of a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped over' turns the horse and 'it' together into TIGAN; 'a' is a link. Terence Rattigan wrote The Winslow Boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was an English dramatist, so a writer of plays.

clue.text: Munro's working as Colin's writer

parts.note: a Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet, a ben, so Munro's gives the plural bens here
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone is compared, as an author, to the short-story writer Munro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munro' suggests Alice Munro or Saki (H. H. Munro), but it is a Scottish peak, called a ben. E. F. Benson wrote the novel Colin (1923).
explanation.definitionFit: E. F. Benson wrote the novel Colin, so he is that book's author.

clue.text: Darling window frames brought about a memoir

indicators.note: brought about means the two words are placed around the next letter

parts.note: angel is a term of endearment, like darling
sashes are the frames of sliding windows

explanation.surface: A beloved window's frames bring a life story about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' places the article between the two pieces. Angela's Ashes is Frank McCourt's memoir of a Limerick childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela's Ashes is Frank McCourt's autobiography of his childhood in Limerick.

clue.text: Quested, say, and brought back a girl seduced by Zeus

indicators.note: brought back means the article and the girl are read in reverse order and spelling

parts.note: Leda was seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan

explanation.surface: Someone went on a quest and returned with one of Zeus's conquests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quested' looks like a verb about questing, but it is Adela Quested of E. M. Forster's A Passage to India; 'say' marks her as an example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adela is the first name of Miss Quested in A Passage to India, so Quested is one bearer of it.

clue.text: Christine Mangan book's point about incense

indicators.note: about tells you one word goes round the other

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point of a fork
to incense is to anger

explanation.surface: A novel's point is said to concern burning perfumed sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' reads as the perfumed smoke but is the verb meaning to enrage; Christine Mangan's 2018 novel is Tangerine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerine is the title of Christine Mangan's debut novel, set in Tangier.

clue.text: A visitor to Combray warns clan he's poorly

indicators.note: poorly means in bad shape, so these letters are disordered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A guest at a French village alerts the family that he feels unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Combray is the childhood village in Proust's In Search of Lost Time, where Charles Swann visits the narrator's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Swann calls on the narrator's family at Combray in Proust's novel, so he is a guest there.

clue.text: Sterne forced to accept small bribe

indicators.note: to accept means one piece takes another into itself
forced means wrenched out of shape, so the novelist's name is rearranged

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Laurence Sterne is pressured into taking a minor bung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges the novelist's name into STENER, and 'to accept' puts the small word inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is slang for a bribe or inducement that makes a deal more palatable.

clue.text: Dramatist using two ways to limit work each year

indicators.note: to limit means the two roads form the bounds round the middle letters

parts.note: street abbreviates to St, one way
road abbreviates to Rd, the second way
op is short for opus, a work
p.a. is per annum, each year

explanation.surface: A playwright uses two routes to cap annual output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two ways' supplies two street abbreviations, one for each road word. Tom Stoppard wrote Arcadia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Stoppard is a British writer of plays such as Arcadia, so a dramatist.

clue.text: Collins heroine's turn, unexpectedly, to eat crust

indicators.note: to eat means one word swallows the other inside it

parts.note: to veer is to turn suddenly and unexpectedly
rind is a hard outer crust, as on cheese

explanation.surface: A Victorian heroine suddenly swerves to bite into a crust.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Verinder is the heroine of Wilkie Collins's The Moonstone; ''s' is a link meaning 'is' or 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachel Verinder, owner of the stolen diamond, is the leading woman in Wilkie Collins's The Moonstone.

clue.text: Play or article, one showing attention to detail

parts.note: the is the definite article
a caretaker takes care, paying attention to the details of a building

explanation.surface: A drama, or a piece of writing, is praised for being meticulous.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Pinter's The Caretaker (1960); 'or' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caretaker is Harold Pinter's 1960 stage drama.

clue.text: Irish princess that is leader of some ancient parts

indicators.note: parts means the letters for that is are split apart to hold something

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: leader of means only the first letter of some

parts.note: old means ancient

explanation.surface: A royal Irish girl leads some archaic regions.
explanation.walkthrough: Isolde is the Irish princess of the Tristan legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Tristan legend Isolde is the daughter of the King of Ireland.

clue.text: Name used by Iris Isherwood's train changer

parts.note: orris is a kind of iris whose root gives orris powder

explanation.surface: A novelist named Iris uses a pseudonym for Isherwood's character who switches trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a writer's first name but is the flower. Isherwood's novel is Mr Norris Changes Trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood's Mr Norris Changes Trains makes Mr Norris the man who switches trains.

clue.text: Proper bible period for Botticelli's work

parts.note: prim means proper, primly correct
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A suitable stretch of biblical history is chosen for a Renaissance painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Primavera is Botticelli's famous painting of spring in the Uffizi.

clue.text: Mentor of a child lost in Lakeland

indicators.note: lost in means the letters sit concealed inside the word Lakeland

explanation.surface: A child's guide goes missing in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Akela is the name of the adult leader of a Cub Scout pack, from the wolf in Kipling's Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela, the pack leader, guides young Cub Scouts, so is a mentor to children.

clue.text: Intro to The Idiot by old Italian poet

indicators.note: intro to means just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: The opening of Dostoevsky's novel is credited to an ancient Italian bard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Idiot' looks like Dostoevsky's title; split it, the first letter of 'The' then ASS for 'Idiot'. Torquato Tasso wrote Jerusalem Delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was a sixteenth-century Italian epic writer of verse.

clue.text: Touchstone's poor virgin regularly ran up the old road backwards

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the words ran up
backwards means the old word for the and the road abbreviation are read in reverse

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A clown's lowly sweetheart jogs up an ancient road in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A and U from 'ran up'; 'backwards' turns YE RD into DREY. Touchstone calls Audrey 'a poor virgin, sir, an ill-favoured thing' in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It the jester Touchstone woos the country girl Audrey, whom he describes as a poor virgin.

clue.text: Little Dubliner who makes things wicked

definitions.meaning: Little ... is the clerk in A Little Cloud in Joyce's Dubliners
a maker of candles gives things wicks, so makes them wick-ed

explanation.surface: A small Irishman is accused of corrupting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' reads as evil but is read as 'given wicks'; Little Chandler is in Joyce's Dubliners.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle maker is traditionally called by this trade name, and Joyce's Little Chandler is a Dubliners character.

clue.text: Lane in Candleford finally used by killers

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of Candleford

parts.note: orcas are killer whales

explanation.surface: A country lane near Candleford is used by murderers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lane' looks like a road but is Dorcas Lane, the postmistress in Flora Thompson's Lark Rise to Candleford.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorcas is the first name of Miss Lane, the Candleford postmistress in Flora Thompson's books.

clue.text: Abstract art uses a god to depict dusk

indicators.note: abstract art bears no literal likeness, so these letters are reshaped into another form

explanation.surface: Non-figurative painting enlists a deity to portray evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abstract art' reads as a painting style, but 'Abstract' is the anagram signal for ART USES A. Astraeus was the Titan of dusk in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Astraeus was the Greek Titan of the evening and the stars, linked with twilight.
